 JUDGMENT
The claimant not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal in MCOP No.1857 of 2017, dated 31.01.2023 has preferred this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.

2.The case of the petitioner is that on 09.03.2017 at about 21.30 hrs, the petitioner was proceeding in a two wheeler bearing Regn. No. TN-22 S-7807 as a pillion rider at Medavakkam Main Road,
Kovilambakkam Opp.to Balaji Medical shop from north to south
, at that time, the driver of lorry bearing Regn. No. TN-07-AM-6085 drove it in a rash and negligent manner from behind, dashed the petitioner's two wheeler and caused an accident.
Due to which, the claimant sustained degloving injury on the left leg, for which he underwent treatment in the hospital.

Under these circumstances,
the claim petition came to be filed before the Tribunal seeking for payment of compensation of Rs.16,00,000/-.

3.The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, came to a conclusion that the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 23/06/2025 01:20:58 pm ) accident had taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the rider of the 1st respondent. Having come to such a conclusion,
the Tribunal fixed the total compensation payable at Rs.3,02,900/- under various heads as follows:
S.No Compensation
awarded
under   the head
1. Disability   2. Pain and sufferings
3 . Transportation   4. Extra nourishment
5. Attender charges   6. Loss of earnings   7. Loss of amenities
Total  4.The above compensation was directed to be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

5. The learned counsel for appellant argues that due to the accident happened on 09.03.2017, the petitioner's left leg toes were amputated, due to which, he was not able to do his mason work and he sustained permanent disability.

Therefore, the multiplier method ought to have been applied by the tribunal, but the tribunal has fixed only a sum of Rs.5000/- per percentage of https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 23/06/2025 01:20:58 pm ) disability as such is erroneous one and prayed for enhancement of compensation.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for 2nd respondent insurance company argues that the tribunal granted the award under various heads is well-reasoned one, which needs no interference.
Hence, he raised strong objections and prayed to dismiss this appeal.

7. On perusal of award passed by the Tribunal below, the fact reveals that at the time of accident, the claimant was the mason and the accident was happened in the year 2017 and he could not attend his work for more than 5 months.

Therefore, on seeing the grievous injury and on considering the cost of living, this Court is inclined to fix the disability at 20% and the notional income is to be enhanced from Rs.10,500/- to Rs.12000/- per month and the multiplier of 17 is to be applied.
The petitioner has undergone surgery and took treatment, due to which he could not attend his work at least for five months.
Hence, this Court is inclined to arrive 5 months for the loss of income and also to enhance the amount arrived by the tribunal for pain and sufferings from Rs.40,000/- to R s .

As he took treatment as inpatient in the Government Hospital, this Court is inclined to enhance the extra nourishment as Rs.20,000/-, the attender charges as Rs.50,000/- and for loss of amenities as Rs.50,000/-.
The compensation that has been fixed under the other heads are reasonable and does not require the interference of this Court.

8.In the light of the above discussion, the compensation awarded by the tribunal is modified as follows:

 (Rs.12000 x 17 (multiplier) x 5 =
 Rs.10,20,000)
 2. Pain and Sufferings   3. Transportation expenses   4. Extra nourishment   5. Attender charges   6. Loss of amenities   Total  https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

sentences.text: The second respondent insurance company is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation of Rs.13,20,000/-, less the amount already deposited, together with interest at 7.5% p.a. from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of this judgment.
Insofar as the enhanced compensation is concerned, the deficit court fee, if not paid, shall be paid by the claimants.
The other directions issued by the Tribunal with regard to the mode of payment of compensation remains unaltered.
10.In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.
